identity.name: Niger Coast Protectorate
alt_names: Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria

land.text: Southern Nigeria, joined to the Northern Nigeria Protectorate in 1914

successors.note: No dossier exists; Cliopatria's British Africa row (1885-1960) draws British Nigeria. 'In 1914, Southern Nigeria was joined with Northern Nigeria Protectorate' (Southern Nigeria page).

capitals.name: Old Calabar
capitals.note: Infobox capital Old Calabar; Eastern Province capital Calabar, Central Province capital Warri (Southern Nigeria page).

correction.text: the Oil Rivers coast: 'the eastern coast of present-day Nigeria' (Niger Delta, Cross River, Akwa Ibom) and the Warri coast, 'in theory ... as far as Lokoja'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives only 'Established: 1884' and the inland limit Lokoja (undated, 'in theory'); no area figure. The Niger Delta region, Akwa Ibom, Cross River and Delta State stand for the coastal states (Bonny, Opobo, Brass, Old Calabar, Warri) under treaties; the inland claim is not drawn.

correction.text: the coast plus the kingdom of Benin, absorbed after the capture of Benin City on 18 February 1897

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Edo State added; 'Benin was absorbed into the British Niger Coast Protectorate'.

correction.text: Southern Nigeria Protectorate from 1 January 1900: the Niger Coast plus the Royal Niger Company's territories south of Lokoja

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'formed in 1900 from the union of the Niger Coast Protectorate' and 'territories chartered by the Royal Niger Company, south of Lokoja'. The Igboland region (Onitsha, Awka) stands for the Company's lower-Niger lands; the page gives no area and says the northern boundary is only 'below Lokoja on the Niger River'.

correction.text: the Aro country and the Igbo hinterland after the Aro Expedition (November 1901 - March 1902)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Abia, Imo, Enugu and Ebonyi added. The Anglo-Aro War page names the Igbo hinterland and four axes of advance (Oguta, Akwete, Unwana, Itu) but no frontier; the four states are the researcher's reading.

correction.text: the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria: the Lagos Colony and its Yoruba protectorate added on 28 February 1906

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'On 28 February 1906, the two territories were amalgamated as the combined territory called the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria.' Lagos, Ogun, Oyo, Osun, Ondo and Ekiti stand for the Lagos Colony and 'a protectorate over most of Yorubaland'.

region.text: the eastern coast of present-day Nigeria and the Warri coast

ledger.note: 1884: the Oil Rivers Protectorate is proclaimed on the Nigerian coast. Infobox 'Established: 1884'; 'originally established as the Oil Rivers Protectorate in 1884 and confirmed at the Berlin Conference the following year'; the Warri chiefs signed a protectorate treaty on 16 July 1884 (Warri page). The page gives the coast, not a boundary.

1886 (February): Bonny comes under the protectorate. 'In February 1886 a protectorate treaty was concluded between Bonny and Britain' (Bonny Kingdom page). The Niger Delta region of the 1884 shape already covers Bonny; the event dates its entry. Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of bonny-kingdom 1886.

1887 (September): Opobo passes under the protectorate. The Opobo page's rulers table ends Jaja I's rule in 'September 1887' and gives the 'Council of Chiefs' after it; it does not name the British. Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of kingdom-of-opobo 1887 (confidence 1, as there).
1893 (12 May): the Oil Rivers Protectorate is renamed the Niger Coast Protectorate. 'It was renamed on 12 May 1893'.
1897 (9 February): the British invade Benin. 'On 9 February 1897, the invasion of the Kingdom of Benin began'.
1897 (18 February): Benin City is captured. 'The capital was captured on 18 February.'
1897 (18 February): Benin is absorbed. 'Benin was absorbed into the British Niger Coast Protectorate and eventually into British colonial Nigeria'; the Oba was deposed and exiled to Calabar.

1900 (1 January): the Niger Coast Protectorate becomes the Southern Nigeria Protectorate. 'formed in 1900 from the union of the Niger Coast Protectorate' (Southern Nigeria page: Established 1 January 1900); the Niger Coast page: 'merged with the chartered territories of the Royal Niger Company on 1 January 1900'.

region.text: the Royal Niger Company's territories south of Lokoja

ledger.note: 1900 (1 January): the Royal Niger Company's southern territories are added. 'On 1 January 1900, the company transferred its territories to the British Government for £865,000. The territory became the Northern and Southern Nigeria protectorates' (Royal Niger Company page); Southern Nigeria absorbed the territories chartered by the Company 'south of Lokoja'. The Igboland region is the researcher's reading of the lower Niger stations (Onitsha).

1901 (28 November): the Aro Expedition leaves. 'On November 28, Lt. Col. Arthur Forbes Montanaro led 87 officers, 1,550 soldiers and 2,100 carriers' in four columns from Oguta, Akwete, Unwana and Itu.
1902 (March): the Aro are beaten. 'Aro dominance crumbled in March 1902'; Arochukwu fell on 28 December 1901.

region.text: the Aro country and the Igbo hinterland

ledger.note: 1902 (March): the Aro country passes to the Southern Nigeria Protectorate. 'By early 1902, the war was over and the Aro Confederacy collapsed' (Aro Confederacy page); the page names the Igbo hinterland, the four states are the researcher's reading.
1906: Lagos becomes the administrative centre. 'Lagos (administrative centre from 1906)'.

region.text: the Lagos Colony and its protectorate over most of Yorubaland

ledger.note: 1906 (28 February): the Lagos Colony and its Yoruba protectorate join Southern Nigeria. 'On 28 February 1906, the two territories were amalgamated as the combined territory called the Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria'; 'the protectorate was incorporated into the Southern Nigeria Protectorate in February 1906'.

1911: Nri's ritual power ends 'in 1911, when an expedition carried out by British colonial troops forced the reigning eze Nri' to renounce the ikenga (Nri Kingdom page). The Igboland region of the 1900 shape already covers it. Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of nri-kingdom 1911.

region.text: Southern Nigeria, to the amalgamated Colony of Nigeria

ledger.note: 1914 (1 January): Southern Nigeria is joined with Northern Nigeria. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1 January 1914'; 'In 1914, Southern Nigeria was joined with Northern Nigeria Protectorate'; Lugard became Governor General of 'the now combined Colony of Nigeria' (1914-1919).

wars.name: Royal Navy against Nana Olomu
wars.outcome: 'In 1894, after a dispute, the Royal Navy defeated Nana Olomu, ending Warri's autonomy and integrating it into the Lagos Colony' (Warri page).
wars.note: The Warri page says Lagos Colony; the Southern Nigeria page makes Warri the capital of the Central Province of Southern Nigeria, so the integration is read as into the Niger Coast Protectorate here; no land change is drawn.

wars.name: British Benin Expedition
wars.outcome: British victory: Benin City captured 18 February 1897 and the kingdom absorbed into the Niger Coast Protectorate.

wars.name: Anglo-Aro War
wars.outcome: British victory: Arochukwu captured 28 December 1901, Aro dominance gone in March 1902.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary: the inland limit is 'in theory' Lokoja, then 'below Lokoja on the Niger River'. The coast and the 1906 Lagos merger are firmer than the interior, which was opened state by state.

sources.title: Niger Coast Protectorate
sources.note: Infobox (1884 - 1 January 1900, capital Old Calabar), Oil Rivers 1884 confirmed at Berlin 1885, renamed 12 May 1893, merged with the Royal Niger Company territories 1 January 1900; no area, no boundaries.

sources.title: Southern Nigeria Protectorate
sources.note: Formed 1 January 1900; Lagos added 28 February 1906; Calabar and Warri provincial capitals; Lagos administrative centre from 1906; disestablished 1 January 1914; northern limit below Lokoja.

sources.title: Royal Niger Company
sources.note: Charter July 1886, revoked 1899, territories transferred to the Crown on 1 January 1900 for 865,000 pounds, becoming the Northern and Southern Nigeria protectorates; no extent.

sources.title: Warri Kingdom
sources.note: Warri protectorate treaty of 16 July 1884; the 1894 defeat of Nana Olomu; the Itsekiri coast.

sources.title: Benin Expedition of 1897
sources.note: 9 February invasion, 18 February capture of Benin City, absorbed into the Niger Coast Protectorate.

sources.title: Anglo-Aro War
sources.note: Aro Expedition November 1901 - March 1902; Arochukwu 28 December; the Igbo hinterland.

sources.title: Lagos Colony
sources.note: Lagos annexed 6 August 1861, colony 5 March 1862, protectorate over most of Yorubaland 1890-1897, amalgamation 28 February 1906.

sources.title: Bonny Kingdom
sources.note: February 1886 protectorate treaty with Britain (added by reviewer af-04-x).

sources.title: Opobo

sources.note: 1911 British expedition against the eze Nri (added by reviewer af-04-x).

notes: The Niger Coast Protectorate has no Cliopatria row (Cliopatria's British Africa, 1885-1960, 33 shapes, af-08, draws British Nigeria as part of an aggregate; the renderers must decide which wins). One dossier covers the chain Oil Rivers Protectorate (1884) -> Niger Coast Protectorate (12 May 1893) -> Southern Nigeria Protectorate (1 January 1900, with the Royal Niger Company's southern lands) -> Colony and Protectorate of Southern Nigeria (28 February 1906, with Lagos), 1884-1914. Seven pages opened (budget 6-14 for a long run of shapes; all are read for other dossiers of this batch). The pages give no area and no frontier: the inland extent, the Igboland and Aro states and the Yoruba protectorate are researcher's readings with named states as stand-ins. Disagreements: the Niger Coast page gives 'Established: 1884' and the 1885 Berlin confirmation but not the June 1885 declaration; the Warri page puts the 1894 integration of Warri 'into the Lagos Colony' while the Southern Nigeria page makes Warri the Central Province capital; Moor's last year 1903 (body) vs 1904 (infobox). Not placed: the coast's treaty states (Jaja of Opobo, Nana of Brohemie, Brass, Old Calabar: no page opened), the north (Northern Nigeria Protectorate, a separate state the RNC dossier names), Nri's 1911 end (the Nri dossier has the loss; the land was already inside the Igboland region). Counterparts needing dossiers: lagos-colony (written in this batch), royal-niger-company (written in this batch), colony-and-protectorate-of-nigeria (not written), northern-nigeria-protectorate.
